output_position_reviews.assessment: Gold + hord has final noun/head hord and a zero ending; the whole is a gold hoard. The witness validly notes isolated N/A and number syncretism.
Heofon + fȳr + dative singular -e gives heavenly fire/lightning; the supplied source cell is not promoted to a complete new paradigm.
Hēah with attested combining hēa- + clif + dative plural -um gives high cliffs; no general h-deletion rule is inferred.
The witness explains lexical meaning limits using the taught purple-cloth and spice examples; composition clues do not license free coinage.
Leornian verb learn → leorn-ung feminine learning/study; suffix and both meanings are correct.
Gefēra masculine companion → gefēr-scipe masculine companionship; omission of citation -a is correctly explained.
Rihtwīs adjective righteous → rihtwīs-nes feminine righteousness; category change is correct.
Īdel adjective empty/void → īdel-nes feminine idleness; the established noun sense is preserved.
The witness explicitly rejects predicting physical emptiness by mechanical English suffix substitution; this matches the lexical caveat.
Heofon noun heaven → heofon-lic adjective heavenly; later agreement is distinguished from adjective formation.
Supplied swīð strong → swīðe very is correctly identified as adjective-to-adverb formation in -e.
Supplied sōð true → sōðlice truly is correctly identified as adverb formation in -lice.
Final e alone cannot distinguish an adverb from nominal/adjectival inflection; clause function and lexical identity matter.
Un- marks opposition: righteousness/unrighteousness.
Tō- has the attested asunder relation: burst/break up or go to pieces.
For- belongs to the whole lexical verb forweorðan perish, distinct from weorðan become.
The witness rejects arbitrary coinage, universal prefix translations, and automatic inheritance of a base verb’s meaning or government.
Rihtwīs → rihtwīsnes is derivation, creating an abstract feminine noun from an adjective.
Rihtwīsnes → rihtwīsnesse is inflection of the same noun, with oblique ss and -e.
In Ic lufie rihtwīsnesse, the noun is feminine accusative singular direct object; translation I love righteousness is correct.
The isolated form can also be genitive or dative singular, so spelling alone does not settle case.
He received goods/property is correct; gōdum is the lexical neuter noun in dative plural, governed by onfōn.

The selected people translation and weak accusative plural adjective are correct. The frozen witness’s isolated feminine-singular alternative is also linguistically possible and is now acknowledged in the key.
Dative government in the first clause and article-conditioned weak agreement in the second are correct; plural endings do not uniquely determine gender.
The witness distinguishes lexical noun from substantival adjective and correctly rejects absence of a following noun as a sufficient category test.
Ðā wǣdlan gesāwon ðā hundas and ðā wunda: correct plural subject/verb and coordinated accusative objects; feminine wunda preserves the corrected noun class.
Ic forlǣte ēow sibbe, and ic forgiefe ðǣm ðearfan ðæt goldhord: both recipients are dative, both things accusative, and all four specified lexemes and plural you are retained.
Ðā wǣdlan gelīefað on God: plural agreement and lexical belief on + accusative are correct; no physical-motion explanation is imposed.
Gemiltsa ðǣm wǣdlan, and sęnd him ðæt gold: both commands singular, mercy recipient dative, sent gold accusative and recipient him dative.

The complete frozen translation preserves all 159 source tokens’ connected sense: proportional danger, separate be ðǣm, tree/storm comparison, cliff collapse, mountains’ penalty, and three final outcomes. Office/woodland/assail it/collapse/thunderbolts are defensible choices. Primary pp156–158 corroborate the text and attached notes.
Opening claim correctly links increasing worldly rank to increasing danger.
First comparison correctly identifies the high spreading tree and its stronger shaking.
Second comparison correctly identifies high cliffs/crags and their sudden violent collapse.
Third comparison correctly identifies mountains/hills and the heavenly assault that penalizes their height.
Human conclusion correctly applies the images to powers, wealth and earthly wonders, retaining ruin/sorrow/nothingness.
First hit refers to the tree and is nominative subject of hlīfað.
Hit after brǣt is accusative reflexive object referring to the same tree.
Hit after bið is nominative subject of the coordinated passive participles, again the tree.
Ðe wiexð on ðǣm wudubearwe is correctly identified as the tree’s relative clause.
Ðæt hit hlīfað … and brǣt hit is correctly identified as the result of growth.
The witness correctly pairs temporal ðonne sęmninga … ðonne bið and also accounts for the initial connective ðonne.
Final ðonne after swīðlicor is comparative than, distinct from the temporal pair.
Se ōðer wudu means the remaining forest/trees, not a second forest; Cook156 note11 directly confirms this.
Both hīe refer to the high cliffs and crags.
Onginnað governs both infinitives feallan and hrēosan; no new finite verb is invented.
The paired infinitives reinforce one collapse; full ðearlice intensifies its violence, with suddenness and destination correctly identified.
Ealdor + derivational -dōm + inflectional -es is correct segmentation of the genitive singular noun.
Ealdordōmes depends on wīte and means the penalty of/for pre-eminence; the mountains’ supremacy is the context.
Eorð- + adjective-forming -lic + agreement -an correctly distinguishes derivation from inflection.
Eorðlican is weak nominative neuter plural with ðās … wundor, these earthly wonders, subject of the final result clause.
Ðā hēan mihta is the first subject; falling and coming to destruction are its reinforced outcome.
Ðisse worulde welan is the second subject; worldly riches become sorrow.
Ðās eorðlican wundor is the third subject; earthly wonders come to nothing.
Ðisse worulde is an internal feminine genitive singular dependent of welan; ðās directly agrees with nominative neuter plural wundor.
Oncnāwan and ongietan is accurately quoted and explained as reinforced understanding rather than separate episodes.
Hrēosað, and feallað, and tō lore weorðað is accurately quoted; reinforced downfall culminating in ruin meets the open repetition task.
Ðū eart dūst, and ðū gewęntst tō dūste preserves person, nominative predicate, contracted verb, and dative endpoint. It matches the key.

All clauses and targets are preserved: swā swīðe, bare middangeard, sealde, supplied weak āncęnnedan Sunu, nān … ne, bare relative ðe, belief on hine, purpose forweorðe/hæbbe and eternal life. Present purpose tense is justified by the continuing intended outcome.

Bare Hǣlend in the witness versus se Hǣlend in the model preserves the taught proper-title referent; no article target applies. Direct speech, three bare nominative predicates, nān … ne, tō + dative and supplied būtan ðurh + accusative are all correct.

Witness fronted objects followed by verb–subject differ from model object–subject–verb, but both orders preserve first-person giving/leaving, accusative sibbe/mīne sibbe, plural dative ēow, required forgiefan, and omission of with.

Witness Ðā rīnde hit versus model Ðā hit rīnde is acceptable narrative order. Rain, explicit ðǣr, plural floods/winds and āhruron, accusative house goal and singular fēoll are all preserved. The shared plural antecedent of fell is implicit in the original prompt.
Both parallel clauses retain singular ǣlc trēo with birð, nominative neuter subject adjectives, masculine accusative plural fruit adjectives and corrected short-æ wæstmas.

The witness matches the final-finite-auxiliary model: bare ðe, singular gōdne wæstm, negation, forcorfen/worpen passive pair, articleless on fȳr and final bið. Ordinary auxiliary-first alternatives can be valid but fail this specified order target.
Past purpose gebǣde and factual gebæd are correctly distinguished, each with accusative hine. Accusative on munt, singular rēaf and hwīt/scīnende description are correct; no progressive is invented.
Se munt, hrēosende, wierð tō nāhte retains the supplied participle, singular present and required nothingness outcome.
The witness matches the model’s dative glory phrase, negative past passive, explicit swā-swā and ān + genitive ðissa.

Witness eall ðæt ðe versus model eall ðæt is a defensible relative variant. All objects, plural dative him, strong dēorwierðu after his, plural spices, dative treasure location and singular gemētt wæs are preserved.
Sum welig mann mid gōdwębbe geglęnged wæs correctly preserves indefinite subject, dative material, past passive and final finite auxiliary target.
Ðā læg sum wǣdla æt his geate has the correct singular subject/verb and supplied static gate phrase with its possessor.

The witness’s geaf matches the repaired selected verb and current §5 frame; recipient placement differs harmlessly. Nān … ne, plural hundas/cōmon/liccodon and accusative feminine his wunda are correct. Model and canonical dependencies now consistently use giefan.
Witness optional anticipatory hit is expressly permitted by local help. Past factual gewāt, plural ęnglas bǣron, accusative hine, supplied genitive Abrahames and dative singular wīce are all correct.
Āhōf and geseah correctly share the singular subject; ēagan is accusative plural, ūp is retained, Abraham is supplied accusative, and feorran needs no added of.
Direct address, singular gemiltsa/sęnd, dative mē and supplied accusative Lazarum exactly satisfy the prompt and targets.
Moving gōdum before onfēnge is acceptable; supplied gemun, factual second-singular preterite, dative received goods and dative lifetime phrase are preserved.

Witness sęnde before the destination differs from the model’s final verb but no final-order target is assigned here. Hālsian accusative addressee, accusative person sent, requested subjunctive and internal genitive mīnes fæder within dative destination are correct.

Witness subject-first consequent versus model inversion is acceptable. Open condition uses plural indicative, each proposition has ne, the prophets are accusative plural, and the supplied concessive ends in ārīse after of dēaðe; no will is added.

Witness nū placement differs harmlessly. Plural tiliað, dative reflexive ēow, genitive frēonda, supplied on Godes ðearfum, plural addressees, accusative manige Lazaras/licgende and dative æt ēowrum gatum all satisfy the task.
